ENGLISH — TERMLY EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

2. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. No full stops
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. Only one word repeated

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. blue
   C. quickly
   D. run

4. When practising Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Nouns and Quantifiers.

5. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only a describing word
   C. Only an action
   D. A person, place, thing, or idea

6. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.

7. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the Library
   C. Where is the library?
   D. Where is the library

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Literature: Short Forms.

9. When practising Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Play: Structure and Setting.

10. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

11. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

12. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. going
   C. went
   D. goes

13. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.

14. When practising Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Play 1.4.1 Play: Structure and Setting.

15. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 11.4.1 Grade - appropriate Play: Lessons learnt and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Mechanics of writing-Abbreviations and Acronyms 12.5.1 The Writing process 13.5. and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 11.5.1 Mechanics of Writing: Abbreviations and Acronyms and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Listening to Respond: Expressing Feelings and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Listening to Respond: Expressing Feelings and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 12.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension Strategies and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
